findings.text: the create case asserts _units(result['uncovered_by_write']) == owed where owed is read from the same result's review_owed, so the two sides come from one call and move together: a regression that made both lists wrong in the same way (for example returning every section rather than every unit the create wrote) would leave this assertion true, and only the separate assert owed keeps it from passing on an empty pair.

the skill case asserts only that 'review_owed' appears somewhere after the first 'uncovered_by_write' occurrence, which holds for any insertion of the term before a later mention; it does not check the claimed ordering of guidance (act on uncovered_by_write after your own write, review_owed before a build), so it would pass on a skill edit that states the opposite rule.

the gate log's '# revision:' header names ce20b61bd while the tree it ran in carried the change before it was committed, so no commit sha identifies the tested content and a reader cannot reproduce the run from the log alone; naming the eventual head commit or recording the dirty-tree state would make the receipt reproducible.
